:::{#def-nat}
#### Nat

A **nat** is the unit of information
when the [logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) in [surprisal](#def-surprisal),
and in every quantity built from it, is the [natural logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-natural-log).

One nat is the surprisal of a [value](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-realization) with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1/\euler$:
for a value $x$ of a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\surprisalf{x} = 1 \text{ nat}
&\iff -\ln \P(X=x) = 1\\
&\iff \P(X=x) = \e{-1} = 1/\euler \approx 0.368.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
